en.a11yChip: {name}. Drag it to a figure, or press to pick it up.
en.a11yBox: An empty box. Drop a name here.
en.a11yZone: The {name} side. Press to sort the shape here.
en.a11yCard: A shape. Swipe it left or right, or press the left or right arrow key.
en.a11ySide: A side of the shape. Tap it to add its length.
en.a11yVertex: A corner of the heptagon. Drag it.
en.p02Warm: Let’s have a quick warm up.
en.w1Ask: Swipe the shape to the side that names the highlighted part.
en.w1Wrong1: Look again! Only the boundary of the square is highlighted. The inside is not shaded.
en.w1Right1: Correct! The boundary of the square is highlighted. The distance around a closed figure is its perimeter.
en.w1Wrong2: Look again! The whole region inside the rectangle is shaded, not just its boundary.
en.w1Right2: Correct! The region inside the rectangle is shaded. The region enclosed by a closed figure is its area.
en.w1Wrong3: Look again! Only the 3 sides of the triangle are highlighted. The inside is empty.
en.w1Right3: Correct! The 3 sides of the triangle are highlighted. The distance around the triangle is its perimeter.
en.w1Wrong4: Look again! This time, the inside of the square is shaded, not only its boundary.
en.w1Right4: Correct! This time, the region inside the square is shaded. So, it shows the area of the square.
en.w1Wrong5: Look again! The whole region inside the triangle is shaded, not only its sides.
en.w1Right5: Correct! The region inside the triangle is shaded. So, it shows its area.
en.w1Done: Well done! You sorted all 5 shapes.
en.w1Identified: We have identified what the perimeter is.
en.b0Intro: Let’s find the perimeter of these shapes.
en.b1Ask: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
en.b1Wrong40: Look again! You multiplied 8 by 5. For perimeter, add the lengths of all 4 sides.
en.b2Ask: What is the perimeter of this square?
en.b2Wrong225: Look again! You multiplied 15 by 15. For perimeter, add the 4 sides.
en.b2Right: Correct! All 4 sides of the square are 15 cm.
en.b3Ask: What is the perimeter of this triangle?
en.b3Wrong45: Look again! 3 × 15 works only if all 3 sides are 15 cm. These sides are not equal.
en.b3Right: Correct! 12 + 9 + 15 = 36 cm. We added each side once.
en.bWrongGeneric: Look again! Add the lengths of all the sides.
en.b4Sum: The sum of all the side lengths gives the perimeter of any polygon!
en.o0Intro: Let’s find out the perimeter of other polygons.
en.o1Ask: Drag each name to its figure.
en.o1Wrong5: Look again! This figure has 5 sides, not {m}.
en.o1Wrong6: Look again! This figure has 6 sides, not {m}.
en.o1Wrong7: Look again! This figure has 7 sides, not {m}.
en.o1Wrong8: Look again! This figure has 8 sides, not {m}.
en.o1Done: Well done! You named all 4 polygons. The number of sides tells us the name.
en.o2Look: Now, let's look at the sides of these polygons.
en.o2Regular: A polygon with all sides and all angles equal is a regular polygon.
en.o3Ask: Is this polygon regular or irregular? Swipe it to the correct side.
en.o3Wrong1: Look again! All 5 sides of this pentagon are the same length.
en.o3Right1: Correct! All the sides and angles of this pentagon are equal. So, it is a regular pentagon.
en.o3Wrong2: Look again! Some sides of this hexagon are long and some are short.
en.o3Right2: Correct! The sides of this hexagon are not all equal. So, it is an irregular hexagon.
en.o3Wrong3: Look again! All 8 sides of this octagon are the same length.
en.o3Right3: Correct! All 8 sides and all the angles are equal. So, it is a regular octagon.
en.o3Wrong4: Look again! The sides of this heptagon have different lengths.
en.o3Right4: Correct! The sides of this heptagon are not all equal. So, it is an irregular heptagon.
en.o3Wrong5: Look again! This pentagon has some longer and some shorter sides.
en.o3Right5: Correct! The sides of this pentagon are not all equal. So, it is an irregular pentagon.
en.o3Wrong6: Look again! All 7 sides of this heptagon are equal, and so are its angles.
en.o3Right6: Correct! All the sides and angles are equal. It is a regular heptagon.
en.o3Done: Well done! You sorted all 6 polygons.
en.o4IrrA: The sides are not all equal.
en.o4Great: Great sorting! Now we know two kinds of polygons. A regular polygon has all sides and angles equal.
en.o4Next: Let's find the perimeter of regular polygons first.
en.r1Start: Let's start with an equilateral triangle. All its 3 sides are equal. Let each side be a.
en.r1TapAsk: Tap each side of the triangle.
en.r1Walk: Let's walk around the triangle. Tap each side to add its length.
en.lblAddSides: Add the lengths of the sides:
en.r1Done: Well done! There are 3 sides, and each side is a. So, the perimeter is 3 × a = 3a. Next, a square!
en.r2Say: A square is a regular polygon too. It has 4 equal sides. So, its perimeter is a + a + a + a = 4a. Next, a regular pentagon!
en.r3Say: Here is a regular pentagon. It has 5 equal sides. So, its perimeter is a + a + a + a + a = 5a.
en.r4Say: Did you notice? The perimeter is the number of sides × a. 3 sides give 3a, 4 sides give 4a. Let's try more polygons!
en.r5Ask: Drag the correct perimeter to each polygon.
en.r5Say: All these polygons are regular. Each side is a. Find the perimeter of each one!
en.r5WrongHex: Look again! A hexagon has 6 sides, not {m}. Hint: Count the sides of each polygon.
en.r5WrongHept: Look again! A heptagon has 7 sides, not {m}. Hint: Hepta means 7 and octa means 8.
en.r5WrongOct: Look again! An octagon has 8 sides, not {m}. Hint: Perimeter = number of sides × a. Count the sides of the octagon.
en.r5Done1: The perimeters are 6a, 7a and 8a. For each polygon, multiply the number of sides by a.
en.r5Done2: Well done! 6 sides give 6a, 7 sides give 7a and 8 sides give 8a. Perimeter = number of sides × length of one side.
en.i0Intro: Let’s find out the perimeter of irregular shapes.
en.i1Ask: Drag any vertex of the heptagon.
en.i1Look: Look! The sides are not equal now. It is an irregular heptagon. To find its perimeter, add the lengths of all its sides.
en.i2Ask: What is the perimeter of this heptagon?
en.i2Wrong28: Look again! 7 × 4 cm works only when all the sides are equal. These sides are not equal.
en.i2Wrong26: Look again! You have left out one side. A heptagon has 7 sides.
en.i2Wrong35: Look again! 7 × 5 cm uses only one side length. The sides are not equal.
en.i2Right: Correct! 4 + 5 + 3 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 5 = 30 cm. So, the perimeter of this heptagon is 30 cm.
en.endDone: Great job! You can now find the perimeter of any polygon!
